note: Capability whitelist for discover. Keys are capability_ids, never directory names (v0.3 §9.3:716). Every entry must carry at least one pe_static predicate unless weak_evidence is declared with a reason. wl-4 (draft §82, decision D9): the `media_probe` entry went with the capability when `cap-2` unfroze it — the load-time check refuses a whitelist entry whose capability is not frozen, which is the check doing its job. wl-5 (draft §121, ADR-0048): `rust-toolchain` gained the recognition half it deliberately lacked in §117 — the ledger has to be able to describe what an installer wrote into the user's directories, and `rustc.exe`'s own PE version resource is what makes that recognisable. The predicate requires **both** the name and the product string on purpose: the shims in `.cargo\bin` carry no version resource at all (measured), so a name-only rule would register three references whose every fact is unreadable. wl-6 (draft §141): the `ffmpeg` capability was frozen and got its entry in the same stage; the machine's build is a `gpl-shared` archive with **no version resource at all**, so this is the second entry (after `build`/cmake) that declares weak evidence rather than a product string, and its version is honestly reported as unknown.

entries.weak_reason: the ffmpeg builds on this machine are `gpl-shared` archives whose PE carries no version resource at all (product, company and file version all absent, measured in draft §141), so the name plus a PE image is the strongest static evidence available and the version is reported as unknown rather than read from a resource that is not there.

cmake ships builds whose version resource is not consistently populated; the executable name plus a PE image is the strongest available static evidence in P2. The capability itself *is* frozen (policy/capabilities.json `cap-4`); what is weak here is the **recognition** evidence, not the capability's existence.

exclusions.reason: GUI application or service; v0.3 §2.3 and §9.6:789 keep these out of the managed lifecycle
Everything is a mechanism reference and performance baseline for the Native Search Extension, never a managed object (v0.3 §12, §21)
package/download caches are Zone W derived data, not capability objects (v0.3 §7.1, §13.3); a cached python.exe is a build artifact, not a runtime
